threatModel.summary: Current authorized repository HEAD 4e10eca69c42211651ca907f38b74b6d19e6928c implements an in-process Rust DOCX comparison, edit, inspection and PDF/PNG rendering engine, exposed through native CLI, Python/PyO3, WASM Node/browser APIs and Node CLI. Python MCP serves document tools over stdio. Bindings disable engine defaults, enabling shared CLI grammar without native self-update. Native rendering additionally accesses host fonts/cache. Release and AI-review workflows exercise separate network/publication authority. No hosted document service or tenant deployment was established (src/lib.rs:7-30; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-40; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381).
assets: Confidential document bytes, revisions/deleted text, comments, metadata, images/fonts, projections and rendered outputs; caller memory, local files and MCP responses carry these assets (src/lib.rs:17-30; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:126-150,185-218).

Source/output integrity and edit intent: optional legacy source_sha256 guard, prepared source/request/output digests, exact anchors and native prepublication source reread (src/edit.rs:2081-2088; src/edit/prepared.rs:196-235; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1655).

Process availability: default admission allows 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB total inflation, 10000 entries and depth 256; comparison/WmlDocument allows 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB total (src/admission.rs:63-99; src/wml_document.rs:50-55).

Filesystem authority: MCP retained root and derived out_dir/{clean.docx,redline.docx,patch.diff,report.json}, optional redline.pdf/page PNGs; ambient CLI destinations; native Markdown resource-root image files; system/user/cloud fonts and persistent font index (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-217; src/publication.rs:146-225; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2858-2878; src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315,3098-3107).

Native executable, release artifacts, optional signing key, GitHub publication tokens, cargo/npm/PyPI credentials and Jules service/token capabilities (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-369; scripts/release.sh:374-380,919,935-954,1069; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:28-50).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted package bytes enter ZIP/XML/DOM and image/font/legacy parsers. Admission checks budgets, header/extent consistency, safe canonical names, duplicate identities, encryption/compression and bounded inflation. Checked XML validates before DOM construction; permissive parse_xdocument deliberately does not enforce policy (src/admission.rs:439-575; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:90-135). Renderer first admits input, normalizes Strict packages, opens PartFs and expands package-contained altChunks (src/convert/mod.rs:769-808).

JSON edit requests cross into mutation: preparation resolves/checks operations and candidate results before returning bytes; legacy SHA-256 guarding is optional, not authentication or approval. Signed/macro-bearing edit packages are refused (src/edit/prepared.rs:196-235; src/edit.rs:2081-2105).

MCP clients share operator --root, default cwd. Startup normalizes root and opens _OutputRoot; actual reads/publication use retained cap-std authority, not merely Python resolve checks. Writes validate relative names, reject output symlinks and require overwrite for conflicts. No tenant separation or human approval is implemented (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-250,431-463).

Native CLI publication grants ambient selected-path authority; Python/Node CLI handlers also own ambient host I/O and do not inherit MCP confinement. Native OutputRoot publication is atomic per file, not across the artifact set (src/publication.rs:168-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-110).

Native Markdown images use --resource-path or input parent (fallback .), decode escapes, reject URL schemes and require canonical containment plus capability-relative read. Python/Node CLIs reject resource_path (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878,2937-2943; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1057-1064; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727).

Native rendering accesses ambient fonts independently of MCP root: macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts; Linux ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/jubarte/fonts; Windows %APPDATA%/jubarte/fonts. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides these. Index defaults to parent(font-directory)/font-index.tsv; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides or empty/off disables it. Cached face paths are read after stamp checks; saves write a sibling filename ending .tsv.<pid>.tmp then rename (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3098-3107,3154-3229).

Explicit native self-update transfers release-publisher authority into executable replacement. Repository/platform/tag, SHA256SUMS.txt and regular-file extraction are configured; RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None leave signature enforcement disabled (src/update.rs:25-48,87-108,186-258,299-321).

Tag-triggered GitHub release consumes build artifacts, optionally signs using step-scoped ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY staged under $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN with exit cleanup, and publishes dist/* using contents:write. Local release additionally publishes cargo/npm/PyPI packages using operator credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,230-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:374-380,919,935-954,1069).

Pinned external Jules review and companion-fix actions have distinct authority. Review gets PR/check writes with enable_approve=false. Companion invocation rejects fork heads, requires configured trusted author/dispatcher arthrod and qualifying events, then sets require_plan_approval=false and AUTO_CREATE_PR. External action internals are absent. Self-hosted CI/docs execute repository code under runner authority (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:17-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:69-92,259-324; .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-48; .github/workflows/docs.yml:76-99).
attackerCapabilities: Document suppliers control package names/metadata, XML/relationships, embedded media/fonts, legacy structures and Markdown text; host environment, chosen trusted roots, release credentials and operator accounts are not implied capabilities.

MCP clients can read/process under-root documents and invoke exposed writes with overwrite=true. Outside-root access would add authority; ordinary inside-root replacement is already granted (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,153-159).

Local path-race or font-index adversaries require write access to the relevant directories/index. Document-only control does not establish that prerequisite (src/publication.rs:146-148; src/convert/font.rs:3154-3229).

Library callers can select permissive parsing, budgets and callbacks; CLI operators already select ambient paths. These choices become boundaries only when a host exposes them to less-trusted callers.

Release-asset publishers can replace archives and adjacent sums; current checksum-only updater provides no independent signature restriction. PR submitters control review context but lack the configured companion invocation authority unless its gates pass (src/update.rs:44-48,245-249; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324).
securityObjectives: Bound untrusted parsing and preserve safe package identities; callers must additionally enforce process CPU/memory limits (src/admission.rs:439-575; SECURITY.md:38-74).

Avoid document-driven network fetching, macro execution and external office processes; confine native Markdown image reads to the caller-selected resource root (src/admission.rs:16-22; src/lib.rs:7-11; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2878).
Confine MCP document I/O, preserve source/intent guards, require explicit replacement and report partial publication accurately; application root checks are not a process sandbox.
Protect executable/release integrity and secret recipients; keep review verdicts separate from human approval and maintain distinct external-action privileges.
assumptions: No supplied user deployment context/model/knowledge base. Resource paths are configuration-derived expressions; actual runtime environment values, permissions, transport exposure and hosting limits were not supplied.

MCP claims tools only touch root, but native rendering also reads fonts and persists the font index outside that root. Document I/O is confined; process-wide confinement is not established (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:5-9,67-108; src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315,3098-3107,3182-3229).

Signing is explicitly staged in docs; current compiled updater uses checksums only. Workflow signing, if provisioned, does not imply these binaries verify signatures (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:44-48,245-249).

SECURITY.md names rdocx-opc 0.2, while consumed manifest dependency is oxml-opc 0.14.2 with quick-xml 0.41/0.42. This is documentation drift, not an advisory finding (SECURITY.md:89-94; Cargo.toml:104-117).
Engine edit refusal is distinct from filesystem publication failure; multi-file commit can be partial (src/publication.rs:168-174).

Remote action internals, self_update dependency internals, actual credentials, registry/tag protections and self-hosted runner isolation remain unverified. Architecture mapping is not audit completion or a vulnerability finding.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with an extreme HTML colspan can exhaust process memory
findings.summary: A small internal HTML altChunk can set a cell colspan to billions. Rendering serializes one XML grid column per span before layout, causing excessive CPU and memory use despite archive admission.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document content can terminate the host operation through extreme allocation. Impact is process availability; remote/shared service exposure is not established and process isolation is advised.
severity.changeConditions: Host memory/CPU limits constrain impact to a worker; a shared service processing without isolation increases operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified input propagation, unrestricted usize span parsing and proportional string-writing loop; no runtime reproduction.

codeEvidence.label: conversion input
codeEvidence.explanation: The shared layout pipeline first admits the package, then expands internal altChunk data before parsing the generated XML.

codeEvidence.label: html expansion
codeEvidence.explanation: Internal chunk bytes become HTML and generated WordprocessingML.

codeEvidence.label: span input
codeEvidence.explanation: The HTML cell span is parsed as usize with a lower bound of one and no maximum.

codeEvidence.label: column count
codeEvidence.code:
let cols = table
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.iter().map(|c| c.span).sum::<usize>())
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1);
        let col_w = 9360 / cols;
codeEvidence.explanation: Spans are summed into the number of output grid columns without a conversion resource bound.

codeEvidence.label: grid allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: The output String grows once per attacker-selected column, before DOM or page raster limits can act.

rootCause.summary: The internal chunk loader passes HTML into html_to_wml. Cell colspan values have no maximum; end_table sums them and emits one gridCol into a growing String for each column. Admission bounds original archive content, while this expansion happens afterward without a generated-byte budget.

findings.remediation: Reject excessive per-cell spans and aggregate column counts using checked arithmetic before serialization, and enforce a conversion-wide generated-byte budget.

limitations: No application execution or runtime reproduction.
No deployment or host resource limits supplied.
validation.summary: Parent confirmed the path in current source. A single representable large colspan suffices; the issue does not rely on integer overflow. Initial archive budgets and later page pixel limits do not bound this loop.

dataflow.summary: DOCX relationship -> altchunk::expand -> html_to_wml -> span -> cols -> repeated gridCol String writes

impact.why: Process availability loss; no code execution or confidentiality gain established.

likelihood.why: A small HTML numeric value reaches the unbounded growth loop.

reachability.summary: Public conversion and render/report APIs enter with_layout; recipient processing of a supplied document is required, host configuration control is not.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX containing an internal HTML altChunk table with a very large colspan and induce PDF/PNG rendering or a layout report.

remediationTests: Excessive colspan refuses before grid generation.
Ordinary spans render; aggregate spans and overflow refuse safely.

Small admitted HTML can force billions of writes/OOM, independent of package XML budgets. Also verified image 0.25.10 load_from_memory uses default 512 MiB per-decode allocation bound; avoid claiming image decode is wholly unlimited. Investigating aggregate expanded image/font retention.

findings.title: Rendering malformed WMF images can retain overlapping text copies until memory is exhausted
findings.summary: WMF payload fields are bounded by the whole image rather than their own record. Repeated short records can each copy tens of kilobytes from following records, turning a small embedded image into gigabytes of retained text.

severity.rationale: An untrusted image can exhaust the processing host's memory/CPU. Impact is process availability, with no remote service exposure or code execution established.
severity.changeConditions: Host process quotas contain the failure; shared processing without isolation increases operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified image reachability, whole-buffer field reads, owned text retention and short-record advancement in current source; no runtime reproduction.

codeEvidence.label: Internal drawing media
codeEvidence.explanation: Document-controlled internal media is handed to decode_image.

codeEvidence.label: Metafile decode
codeEvidence.explanation: The image path dispatches bytes to the metafile parser and retains its returned text.

codeEvidence.label: Outer WMF size check
codeEvidence.explanation: The check bounds the record extent but payload reads continue using the entire file.

codeEvidence.label: Both WMF text operations
codeEvidence.explanation: Count-based text and coordinate reads can cross the declared record into following records.

codeEvidence.label: Polygon operations
codeEvidence.explanation: Polygon and polypolygon counts likewise read whole-file data without record-local boundaries.

codeEvidence.label: Polyline and advancement
codeEvidence.explanation: Polyline reads whole-file coordinates while the parser advances only by declared record bytes.

codeEvidence.label: Owned text copies
codeEvidence.explanation: Every accepted overlapping string becomes a distinct retained MetaText allocation.

codeEvidence.label: EMF record-local checks
codeEvidence.explanation: The sibling EMF point reader checks each point against the declared record extent.

rootCause.summary: raster_wmf verifies only that each declared size fits in the remaining file. TEXTOUT and EXTTEXTOUT then resolve count-sized strings and coordinates against data, not a slice of that record, and retain owned MetaText. The cursor advances by the small declared size, allowing subsequent records to reinterpret and copy overlapping bytes. POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE share the same missing record-local boundary.

findings.remediation: Parse each WMF record exclusively through a slice of its declared extent, validate count-derived payload lengths before allocation, and impose aggregate retained-text and operation budgets.

limitations: No hostile WMF construction or application execution.
Exact memory and timing thresholds unmeasured.
validation.summary: Parent checked a nonzero placeable bounding box reaches raster_wmf. A short TEXTOUT record with a large u16 text count can read following records, provided trailing bytes cover its text/coordinates. ansi_text materializes owned nonblank Strings before any later failure. The 384-pixel canvas cap bounds raster dimensions, not retained text or record work. Rust whole-file bounds prevent a memory-safety read beyond the input, but do not enforce record framing.

dataflow.summary: Drawing relationship -> decode_image -> metafile::render -> raster_wmf -> whole-file text slices -> ansi_text -> retained MetaText
dataflow.source: Untrusted embedded WMF record sizes and counts
dataflow.sink: wmf_text String conversion and texts retention
dataflow.outcome: Amplified CPU/memory consumption and possible process termination

likelihood.why: Declared record length is not used by the payload parsers.

reachability.summary: The normal drawing/media path reaches the parser; attacker needs only document media control and recipient processing.
reachability.entrypoint: PDF/PNG/layout rendering of internal drawing media

attackPath.summary: Supply an internally referenced placeable WMF with many undersized count-bearing text records and sufficient following bytes, then induce DOCX rendering.

remediationTests: Undersized TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT refuses before text retention.
POLYGON/POLYPOLYGON/POLYLINE counts cannot consume following records.
Valid WMF and EMF rendering remains supported.

originalCandidate.originalEvidence: WMF record parsers validate size2 <= remaining bytes (metafile.rs:477-489) but all payload reads use whole data, never off..off+size2. META_TEXTOUT (614-619) permits a size=4-word (8-byte) record carrying n=65535, then reads text and coordinates from following records; off advances only 8 bytes (684). Repeating these short records makes overlapping ~64KiB strings retained as MetaText per record (wmf_text 692-715, texts Vec 474) -> ~8GiB strings from ~1MiB WMF before layout. META_EXTTEXTOUT (603-610), POLYGON (628-639), POLYPOLYGON (644-660), POLYLINE (663-679) similarly cross record boundaries. EMF read_emf_points correctly bounds p against off+size (1061-1082), useful counterevidence. No app execution/input construction done.

surfaces.label: DTD admission versus permissive DOM tokenization

deferred.reason: Baseline candidate awaiting dependency tokenization confirmation and parent source validation.

candidate.originalEvidence: DOCX admission ignores Event::DocType (src/admission.rs:795-819; Ok(_) => {}), while permissive DOM parse_document skips any ' (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:539-543) and recursively parses remaining '<' elements (550-552, 562, 660-663) with no depth cap. A well-formed main XML prefixed by ' and matching '' then ">]> hides all nested tags inside a DTD entity value from quick-xml's depth scan. Permissive parser skips to ELEMENT's >, then skips to first 's > inside ENTITY, then recurses into remaining '' tags, causing stack overflow before document root. WmlDocument::from_bytes admission (src/wml_document.rs:50-58) -> main_document parse_xdocument (94-102) gives supported entry point. Strict validate_xml rejects DTD but WmlDocument route uses admission and unchecked parse. Verifying dependency DocType scanning statically now; no code execution.
